analysis: What changed vs the 8 AM brief: the tape partially stabilized off the morning lows — the S&P recovered from -1.2% to -0.77% by 10:35 AM ET and the Dow flipped green (+0.27%), led by Nike (+5%+) and Salesforce (+4%+), while the Nasdaq stayed deeply red (-1.7%) as the chip unwind continued. Nvidia deepened to -8.2% (~$151.48, low $150.50), giving back roughly a third of Monday's $39.52 gain, and Anthropic fell further to -14% (~$77.75), now clearly below its $83 IPO price with its market cap down to $1.16T from $1.5T at listing. The VIX eased from 29.34 to ~28.0 and the 10-year held at 4.91%, so the fear gauge is cooling slightly even as chips keep falling — a split that says the stress is sector-specific, not systemic. Two new fundamental items landed: Sanofi's $41B all-cash Insmed deal (biggest biotech deal in nearly three years, powering the biotech/health-care outperformance) and the Commerce Department's Entity List move against Alibaba's Apex unit and six Megaspeed affiliates, effective Nov 25, which ties the Nvidia chip-diversion probe directly to US-China trade friction. Signal vs noise: the broadening chip selloff (ADI -19%, Astera Labs -15%, XSD near a death cross), Anthropic under its IPO price, and the Entity List escalation are signal; the exact midday percentages and the Dow's flip-flopping around flat are noise. The next real tests are FOMC minutes at 2 PM ET and Dell after the close, then Wednesday's PCE/GDP dump before the Thanksgiving break.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Stocks partially stabilize off morning lows: S&P 500 -0.77% at 7,181.29 (from -1.2% mid-morning), Dow flips green +0.27% at 49,729.13, Nasdaq still down -1.70% at 23,679.47.
headlines.why_it_matters: The giveback is pausing, not reversing — the Dow flipping green on Nike and Salesforce shows rotation into non-AI names while the Nasdaq stays pinned by chips.

headlines.headline: Nvidia deepens to -8.2% at ~$151.48 (intraday low $150.50) after Monday's 31.5% surge to $165.05; the stock has now given back roughly a third of Monday's $39.52 gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: Profit-taking is accelerating into the lunch hour, not fading — the reinstatement rally is being retraced fast while the SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline and Dec 1 House testimony still hang over the name.

headlines.headline: Anthropic plunges ~14% to about $77.75, below its $83 IPO price, on pace for a third straight down session since Thursday's debut; market cap down to $1.16 trillion from $1.5 trillion at listing.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's newest public name is now under water vs its IPO price within a week — the cooling is spreading from hardware to AI software names.

headlines.headline: Chip selloff broadens further: Analog Devices -19%, Astera Labs -15%, Micron -10.5%, AMD -10%; SOXX and the Roundhill Memory ETF each -8%+; XSD -8% and near a death cross (50-day about to undercut the 200-day).
headlines.why_it_matters: Sector-wide unwind, not a single-name move — the whole AI hardware complex is retracing Monday's surge together, and the death-cross watch on XSD adds a technical pressure point.

headlines.headline: Sanofi to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash at $175 per share — a ~17% premium to Monday's close (46% to the Nov 18 unaffected price) — the biggest biotech deal in nearly three years; Insmed +14-15%, expected to close in H1 2027 and be EPS accretive by end of 2028.
headlines.why_it_matters: A real M&A catalyst behind biotech's outperformance (XBI +3%+) — deal flow is a counterweight to the tech selloff and a read on pharma appetite for respiratory assets ahead of patent expirations.

headlines.headline: US Commerce Department added Alibaba's Singapore unit Apex Enterprise Solutions and six Megaspeed affiliates to the Entity List, effective Nov 25, over suspected diversion of Nvidia AI chips to China; Alibaba disputes it and says it will seek legal avenues; Susquehanna cut Alibaba's price target to $145 from $190, keeping a Positive rating.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Nvidia chip-diversion probe now has direct trade-policy teeth — tighter export controls add a US-China friction headwind for the AI complex and for Alibaba's cloud growth.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps split: Apple +0.85-1.0% and Microsoft slightly higher, Tesla flipped to +0.7% after an early -1.7%; Amazon -1.45%, Alphabet -1%, Meta roughly flat. Dow leaders Nike +5%+ and Salesforce +4%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: The least AI-exposed mega-caps and Dow value names are holding up while AI-linked names fall — rotation, not a broad risk-off day.

headlines.headline: BNP Paribas cut its Micron rating, citing risks to 2028 hyperscaler capacity plans.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If real, a broker downgrade on capacity-plan risk adds a fundamental (not just technical) leg to the memory-chip selloff; Micron is already -10%+ today.

headlines.headline: Bitcoin down to ~$60,100 (-1.8%); gold futures -1.2% at ~$3,610 after surging 3%+ Monday; WTI crude +0.1% at $80.25.
headlines.why_it_matters: Risk assets are giving back Monday's bounce across the board — crypto and gold falling with stocks while oil steadies.
